ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all founders, council members (Consejo de la Fundacion), protectors, anintended beneficiaries against (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the Panamanian Unidad de Analisis Financiero (UAF) national blacklist; (iv) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; and (v) local and international Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) lists. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is triggered by any PEP designation or high-risk jurisdiction nexus. Any match or red flag requires Suspicious Transaction Report (STR/ROS) filing with the UAF in accordance with Law 23 of 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Publico de Panama - online name search and reservation platform (www.registro-publico.gob.pa; TEPA/eServicios electronic filing system)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the official legal language. Trade names of a Private Interest Foundation may be expressed in a foreign language if rendered in Latin script, but the registry and notary require a Spanish-language statement of intent. The name must not be identical or phonetically similar to an existing registered entity and must not contravene public order or morality. For foundations, the name must clearly distinguish the entity from a public-interest foundation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The reservation may be renewed once for an additional 30 days. Upon rejection, the applicant or the resident agent files a written 'Recurso de Reconsideracion y Apelacion en subsidio' with the Director General of the Registro Publico within five business days of notification, attaching legal arguments and the original reservation receipt. If reconsideration is denied, the administrative appeal is remitted to the appellate registral authority; the final judicial remedy is a writ of annulment (demanda contencioso-administrativa) before the Sala Tercera (Third Administrative Chamber) of the Supreme Court of Justice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible strictly as a statutory registered address maintained at the resident agent's licensed office; however, the industrial quick-freezing operation requires a physical plant with municipal operating permit, Ministry of Health (MINSA) sanitary clearance, and Ministry of Labor (MITRADEL) registration. The Private Interest Foundation may lawfully hold the factory asset and lease real estate, but the pre-incorporation commercial substance plan cannot rely solely on a virtual office for the underlying manufacturing activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registered agent's statutory office: low risk, estimated annual probability below 10% absent an AML/CFT compliance trigger. Actual industrial plant: high risk, estimated above 80% within the first operating year due to mandatory MINSA sanitary inspections, MITRADEL labor visits, municipal environmental review, and potential UAF or Public Registry inspection of the resident agent's KYC records. Sector risk for frozen food processing is classified Low_Risk_Standard but remains subject to unannounced food-safety inspections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama; electronic portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (Sistema Integrado de Gestión de Ingresos - SIGI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign entity, the statutory TIN/RUC is obtained by: (1) securing municipal Aviso de Operación in the relevant district if any commercial operations are conducted in Panama; (2) filing the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) application with DGI through SIGI using notarized constitutional documents, foreign entity certificate of existence, proof of registered local address, and identification of the local legal representative; (3) receiving the provisional RUC and final RUC after DGI validation; (4) completing ITBMS registration and, where applicable, registration as a withholding agent. Non-resident entities may act through a licensed Panamanian law firm or resident agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope; Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is an entity-level taxpayer only for Panamanian-source income, while foreign-source and non-Panamanian activities remain outside the tax net.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch elections. Available elections include: election by eligible small taxpayers to be taxed under the simplified small-taxpayer ITBMS regime (pequeño contribuyente), election to register or not as an ITBMS withholding agent, and optional registration for electronic invoicing once the taxpayer exceeds the mandatory threshold. The PIF civil-law tax classification is fixed by Panamanian Private Interest Foundation Law No. 25 of 1995.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), a VAT-type tax on goods and services; excise duties are separately governed by the unified tax code.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general monetary threshold exists for ITBMS registration; all persons or entities engaging in commercial, industrial, or service activities in Panama must register. Small taxpayers with annual gross turnover not exceeding PAB 36,000 may use the simplified small-taxpayer registration, but this is not a registration exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has progressively mandated real-time electronic invoicing through DGI-authorised electronic billing systems. Registered businesses must transmit XML/JASON-structured invoices to the DGI platform (SIGI) or through certified facturación electrónica suppliers; each invoice receives a DGI-validated digital stamp (QR code/hash) that must be incorporated before issuance to the buyer. Taxpayers above the DGI annual revenue threshold, and all businesses in high-controlled sectors, are subject to mandatory online clearance of each invoice; other registered taxpayers use DGI-preauthorised sequential invoice forms. Non-compliance with real-time clearance can suspend operating registration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS zero-rating may be claimed by registered taxpayers for: (a) tangible movable goods physically exported from Panama, where export is evidenced by customs documentation; (b) services rendered entirely abroad or used exclusively outside Panama by non-resident recipients; (c) sales to legally established free zones, Colon Free Zone concessionaires, Panama-Pacifico special economic area, and international transport services. The exporter must maintain documentary proof that the goods left Panamanian customs territory and that the service was consumed outside Panama; zero-rating is denied if the goods are consumed domestically or repatriated without customs re-entry.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera - DUA) endorsed with the exit stamp
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical shipment
Commercial Invoice/Factura Comercial satisfying DGI and customs requirements
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-bank SWIFT credit proof showing settlement of the export sale
Product movement or consumption certificate where the goods transited through a third country
Certificate of Origin (COO) if required to substantiate export treatment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI conducts post-clearance export audits and cross-checks customs declarations, banking credits, and bills of lading. Fraudulent zero-rating or refund claims trigger: (a) provisional disallowance and clawback of all claimed zero-rated ITBMS benefits; (b) monthly interest surcharges on taxed amounts at the statutory rate; (c) fines ranging from 1 to 3 times the evaded tax; (d) immediate suspension of the RUC and export invoicing privileges; and (e) criminal liability for tax fraud against the legal representative or director. Directors and shareholders of a Panamanian PIF may be jointly liable for amounts clawed back if they actively participated in the fraudulent export scheme.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — sole prudential and AML/CFT supervisor of the banking system; Banco Central de Panamá — statutory creation enacted in November 2022 and still in phased implementation, with monetary functions operationally delegated to the SBP, the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), and Banco Nacional de Panamá (BNP) as fiscal agent of the State; legal tender is the United States Dollar, making the U.S. Federal Reserve the de facto monetary anchor; the national unit of account, the Balboa (PAB, ISO 4217), circulates exclusively as coinage at a fixed 1:1 parity with USD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full, unrestricted convertibility on both current and capital account. Panama has been in continuous compliance with IMF Article VIII since 1970 and maintains no exchange-control statute, no currency licensing, and no tax or quota on inward or outward transfers of dividends, royalties, interest, loan principal, or equity capital. The US Dollar and Balboa are perfectly interchangeable and effectively USD. Practical friction arises only from standard bank-level compliance filters: beneficial-ownership disclosure, RUC tax clearance, sanctions screening, and source-of-funds documentation; none of these operate as a legal convertibility barrier, and no prior central-bank authorization is required for any transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no exchange surrender, no statutory repatriation deadline, and no mandatory conversion ratio on export earnings. Export receipts may be retained in USD, held offshore, or converted to any convertible currency at the exporter's discretion. Administrative obligations are limited to filing the customs export declaration through the national single window (VUCE/SICE) and retaining the commercial invoice, bill of lading, and sanitary export certificates issued by MINSA and AUPSA (and the US FDA/FSMA compliance dossier for shipments to the United States). The collecting bank validates these documents when crediting proceeds, but no deposit or conversion quota is triggered.

Capital Escrow Account; Operational USD Current Account and Payroll Account
Operational USD Current Account; Cash-Covered Documentary Credit Escrow Account
Operational USD Current Account; Trust Escrow Deposit (Cuenta en Fideicomiso)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for domestic fintech wallets; Low for offshore digital EMIs. Panama does not issue a standalone e-money institution (EMI) license; payment and e-wallet undertakings must operate through a licensed bank, a trust structure, or the SBP's Ventanilla de Innovación Digital sandbox. Domestic fintech platforms (e.g., Cobre from Banco General, Tuyo from Banistmo, Walrus from Grupo Ficohsa) can host operating sub-wallets for domestic USD clearing and payroll but lack documentary credit, escrow, and FX hedging capability. Offshore EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, Mercury) generally refuse Panamanian Private Interest Foundation entities, fail to provide USD local-clearing rails, or invoke enhanced due diligence due to Panama's June 2024 FATF grey-list monitoring. Recommended architecture: a licensed Tier-1 commercial bank as the structural primary bank and a domestic fintech wallet only as a limited-float petty-cash and domestic collection pocket.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one natural person — the Founder or a Foundation Council member holding signatory authority — must undergo a live identity interview, either at a physical branch or, under the written policy of most Tier-1 banks, via an SBP-compliant supervised videoconference with digital notarial attestation. Fully remote onboarding without any interview is not available for a PIF holding an active industrial company. Every non-attending signatory must execute a notarized power of attorney legalized by apostille or Panamanian consular certification; the Registered Agent cannot serve as account signatory due to conflict-of-interest rules. Banks typically also inspect or require photographic proof of the factory, the municipal operating permit, and a business continuity assessment before file approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation (PIF) as direct owner of an active trading company — money-laundering overlay risk because foundation beneficiaries are statutorily confidential under Law 25 of 1995.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed beneficiary-disclosure waiver in favor of the bank; proof of filing of the beneficial-ownership return in the DGI/RUC register under Law 254 of 2021; certified copy of the Foundation Deed (Testimonio); Articles/Bylaws; Public Registry certificate; Foundation Council resolution authorizing account opening and signatories; source-of-wealth declaration covering the endowment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pre-revenue factory with no audited financial statements — perceived tax evasion or unreported income risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 24-month cash-flow projection; opening balance-sheet attestation by a licensed CPA; paid pro-forma invoices and purchase orders for machinery; industrial lease or title deed; payroll plan; letters of intent from frozen-food distributors in target export markets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border USD wire patterns to and from high-sanctions-risk jurisdictions, notably PRC-based suppliers for equipment and ingredients, plus potential round-trip funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed OFAC, UN, and EU sanctions screening of all counterparties; 7-day advance notice of first flows to the compliance officer; board minutes authorizing each transfer batch; invoice-pack integrity (commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, insurance certificate); commitment to maintain a minimum 90-day operating balance and to avoid same-day in-out wiring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the registered address (Registered Agent in Panama City) and the physical industrial plant — shell-company red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Industrial lease or title deed; municipal Aviso de Operación; MINSA sanitary operating permit (Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento); AUPSA registration for food-processing imports; payroll lists; geo-tagged photographs or video tour of the production line.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash proximity in food manufacturing — wholesale cash sales and petty-cash float creating unverifiable funds-flow risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-only collection policy; POS or bank-transfer references for all sales; written cash-declaration procedure aligned with the UAF USD 10,000 cash-report threshold; petty-cash policy capped at USD 500 weekly with signed reconciliations; segregation of duties between cash handler and ledger preparer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Endowment and equity injections must be routed as SWIFT MT103 wires from the Founder's pre-existing corporate or personal bank account into the PIF's escrow and operating accounts at the Panamanian bank. SWIFT Field 70 (Remittance Information) must read 'APORTE DE CAPITAL – FUNDACION [NAME] – RUC [NUMBER]' and the bank will map the transaction to the IMF BPM6 statistical category 'Direct Investment – Equity' (A.5.1.1); no Panamanian tax, withholding, or exchange-control declaration applies to capital injections. Recommended pre-funding sequence: (i) compliance risk profile call with the bank's AML officer; (ii) Foundation Council resolution fixing per-transfer limits; (iii) source-of-funds evidence comprising six months of bank statements and prior-year tax returns; (iv) initial wires capped at USD 500,000 each subject to a 24-hour validation hold; (v) full identification of the beneficiary for every correspondent bank. Domestic credits between Panama accounts clear through the SIP RTGS or ACH Panamá within 2-4 business hours, while international USD credits clear via the bank's U.S. correspondent (typically Citi, JPMorgan, or Bank of America) on the Fedwire or CHIPS network.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails hierarchy for the frozen dim sum factory: (i) domestic suppliers and payroll — internal transfer or ACH Panamá/SIP RTGS for same-day settlement in USD; (ii) international suppliers of ingredients, packaging, and consumables — SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer with 3-5 business days of USD clearing via the U.S. correspondent, using the trade purpose code 'Payment for imports of goods – machinery and food inputs' mapped to the BPM6 goods-import category; (iii) capital equipment and large ingredient contracts — Commercial Documentary Letter of Credit, sight or usance 90-180 days, issued under UCP 600 against 100% cash cover for the first 12 months and later against an approved facility, with full document sets (B/L, packing list, commercial invoice, certificate of origin, sanitary certificates); (iv) receivables financing — export factoring of the PIF's invoices using the 'Factura Cambiaria' instrument permitted under Panamanian factoring legislation. Every outbound disbursement requires a supporting pack of pro-forma invoice, purchase order, transport document, SICE customs declaration, and MINSA/AUPSA health certificates for food inputs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR outright forward (spot-plus-forward) up to 12 months against an SBP-licensed counterparty under an ISDA or Panamanian master agreement.
USD/CNY non-deliverable forward (NDF) up to 6 months, cash-settled against the offshore CNH/USD fixing, used because the CNY is not deliverable in Panama.
Cross-currency swap (fixed-for-fixed USD/EUR or USD/CNH) for amortizing term-debt, typically with a USD 1,000,000 minimum ticket.
Plain-vanilla FX swap (tom-next and spot-forward rolling) for working capital in EUR or other trade currencies.
Zero-cost collar or participating forward on USD/EUR for predictable quarterly export conversions, permitted on a hedge-only basis.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Declaration and Payment (Private Interest Foundation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before June 15 of the current calendar year; first payment due by June 15 of the year following initial registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge on the unpaid tax plus monthly statutory interest; failure to pay for two consecutive years causes Public Registry delinquency flagging and administrative strike-off proceedings, resulting in loss of juridical personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta) for Panamanian-source taxable income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the year immediately following the close of the calendar fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-filing surcharge on the tax due, monthly interest on arrears at the statutory rate, and fines up to USD 1,000; persistent non-filing may result in administrative determination and judicial enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficiary Declaration (UBO Reporting) under Law 254 of 2021
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Final Beneficiary Registry (SIBENE), Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the last calendar day of the month following the foundation's registration anniversary, with a supplementary update within 15 days of any beneficial ownership change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative monetary penalties of up to USD 2,000 for the foundation and up to USD 10,000 for the resident agent; suspension of the good-standing certificate until full compliance is achieved.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a Panamanian certified public accountant is required if the Foundation's total gross assets at year-end exceed USD 2,000,000 or its annual Panamanian-source gross income exceeds USD 3,000,000. Such audit is also required if ordered by the DGI or Public Registry for regulated activities; otherwise audit is voluntary.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para las PYMES) applies to small- and medium-sized foundations; full IFRS applies when quantitative thresholds for large entities are met. Books must be maintained in Spanish and expressed in United States dollars (balboa equivalent).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 254 of 2021, the Foundation must file an annual UBO declaration with the DGI Final Beneficiary Registry. The declaration must be updated within 15 days of any transfer of economic foundation interests, assignment of beneficial entitlements, change in foundation council membership, or appointment of a new protector or beneficiary. A nil report is not accepted; the Foundation must confirm the UBO status annually even if no change has occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and Legal Beneficial Owners (Member Register equivalent)
Register of Foundation Council Members and Protector (Director Register equivalent)
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% marginal rate for annual taxable profits exceeding USD 1,500,000; progressive brackets apply below that threshold: 15% on the first USD 11,000, 25% on the slice from USD 11,001 to USD 50,000, and 28% on the slice from USD 50,001 to USD 1,500,000 (Law 134 of 2021 reforms).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial regime exempts foreign-source income; for the quick-freezing factory, income from sales and manufacturing conducted inside Panama is Panamanian-source and taxable, while dividends, interest and royalties received from foreign assets held by the PIF qualify for exemption. The 4% advance dividend tax mechanism reduces the dividend withholding on distributions from 10% to 5%. No general tax holiday applies to ISIC 1074 frozen-food production; capital expenditures may be deducted through depreciation under Fiscal Code rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 851 (Declaración Jurada Anual de Impuesto Sobre la Renta), submitted electronically through the DGI Sede Electrónica portal at https://eservicios.dgi.gob.pa; companies must register for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), obtain an Aviso de Operación and employer registration prior to filing. Quarterly advance income-tax payments are made through the same portal before the final annual filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Form 851); quarterly advance payments of estimated corporate income tax are due during the fiscal year in accordance with DGI instructions for medium and large taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year enterprises, the Form 851 filing window opens on the first business day of January and closes on 31 March of the following year; the DGI commonly extends the deadline to 15 April by published resolution. The quarterly advance payments are payable on the statutory period-end dates indicated on the DGI portal and cannot be carried past 31 March without surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from Panamanian-source commercial and industrial activity; for the PIF factory this includes all domestic and export sales of quick-frozen dim sum and dumplings (ISIC 1074).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident owned PIF must hold a valid Panamanian RUC and Aviso de Operación; report all invoiced sales with supporting export documentation and freight terms (FOB/CIF) for cross-border sales to treaty jurisdictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income excluded from the Panamanian taxable base under the territorial principle.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only income genuinely sourced abroad, such as interest on foreign bank deposits or dividends from non-Panamanian subsidiaries, and attach bank statements and source certificates demonstrating that the underlying activity occurred outside Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total allowable deductions: raw materials, labor, freezing and refrigeration energy costs, depreciation on plant and machinery, freight, insurance, and general operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only with valid invoices and accounting records maintained in Panama; payments to foreign affiliated suppliers above USD 1 million require an arm's-length transfer pricing analysis attached to the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after application of the 5-year tax loss carry-forward and statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the loss carry-forward only where the loss year return was timely filed; a PIF that was dormant in prior years cannot retroactively claim losses for periods before it commenced the factory activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-reference to the Transfer Pricing Annex (Anexo de Precios de Transferencia) and summary of related-party transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when annual gross revenue or net equity exceeds USD 10 million or when related-party cross-border transactions exceed USD 1 million in the fiscal year; non-filing triggers automatic price adjustments and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund due after quarterly advances, foreign tax credits, and the 4% dividend advance tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any outstanding balance blocks the issuance of the Paz y Salvo tax clearance certificate, which is mandatory for the subsequent repatriation of dividends and for renewals of the Aviso de Operación.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 851 attracts an administrative fine between B/. 50 and B/. 5,000 plus a surcharge of 5% of the unpaid tax for each month of delay, capped at 25%, together with moratorium interest of 1% per month; a fraudulent or false return imposes a fine of 100% of the evaded tax and criminal prosecution under Article 280 of the Criminal Code, including travel bans and asset attachment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax applies to dividends distributed to shareholders of registered shares out of Panamanian-source taxable income. The rate drops to 5% where the PIF timely paid the 4% advance dividend tax (pago directo) on its taxable profits. Dividends distributed out of exempt foreign-source income without proper attribution are subject to a 20% withholding rate, and bearer-share distributions carry a 20% rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's comprehensive double tax agreements (including treaties with Mexico, the Netherlands, Singapore, Spain, the United Kingdom, the UAE and South Korea) typically reduce the dividend withholding rate to 5-15%. The PIF must: (i) obtain a Certificate of Fiscal Residence (TRC) and a beneficial-ownership declaration from the foreign shareholder, notarized and legalized as applicable; (ii) submit an application for treaty relief to the DGI (Solicitud de Aplicación del Tratado) before the distribution date; (iii) obtain a prior DGI resolution authorizing the reduced rate; and (iv) file the dividend withholding return showing the treaty rate. Relief is denied to shell vehicles or shareholders without economic substance in the treaty jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% withholding on interest paid to non-residents where the loan was executed and the capital is used outside Panama; Panamanian-source interest is subject to a 12.5% gross-basis withholding unless a treaty reduces or eliminates it. Royalties: 0% for IP exploited entirely abroad; Panamanian-source royalty income paid to a non-resident licensee is subject to a 12.5% gross withholding, with treaty rates typically 5-10% subject to TRC submission and DGI approval.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 10,000,000 in annual gross revenue OR USD 10,000,000 in net equity triggers the mandatory filing of the Transfer Pricing Annex with Form 851; a full comparability study (Local File) is required whenever aggregate related-party cross-border transactions reach USD 1,000,000 in a fiscal year, including purchases of frozen seafood, wheat-flour wrappers and seasoning ingredients from affiliated foreign suppliers and sales to offshore distributors.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Law 254 of 2021 and DGI implementing resolution) apply to PIFs and corporations engaged in relevant activities. The PIF operating an ISIC 1074 industrial quick-freezing plant must demonstrate in Panama: physical production premises with the quick-freezing line, resident operational employees, local board or foundation council meetings with effective decision-making, and books and records kept in Panama. The annual economic substance declaration must evidence staffing, expenditures and premises; failure to comply triggers fines up to B/. 1,000,000, denial of territorial-source exemption, and reclassification of the PIF as a conduit for treaty and CFC purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional misreporting of Panamanian-source sales, over-declaration of foreign-source exemptions, destruction of invoices and production records, or issuance of false purchase receipts for the frozen-food plant.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine equal to 100% of the evaded tax, 25% late-payment surcharge, 1% monthly moratorium interest, confiscation of goods in customs and closure of the production facility; criminal conviction under Article 280 of the Criminal Code carries imprisonment of 2 to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and foundation council members are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax; the DGI may impose preventive travel bans, attachment of personal bank accounts, and civil restitution orders before final judgment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PIF holding the factory as a paper vehicle with no Panamanian staff, no physical freezing plant, no board meetings held in Panama, or nominee officers exercising no control, while continuing to claim territorial exemption and treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the entire foreign and domestic income at the statutory rate with a 38-50% surcharge (100% in fraud cases); ESR fine up to B/. 1,000,000; suspension of the beneficial-owner registration and potential cancellation of the foundation by the Public Registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Judges may pierce the PIF veil, holding directors personally liable for all reassessed tax and penalties and imposing travel restrictions and disqualification from directorship in Panama for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to disclose ultimate beneficial owners to the Custodian Registry under Law 52 of 2016 as amended; undocumented SWIFT LC or TT-Wire flows from foreign buyers without KYC files; or processing of large cash payments from restaurant distributors without AML verification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to B/. 10,000 for late UBO filings and up to B/. 50,000 for false declarations; serious AML violations under Law 23 of 2015 attract fines up to B/. 5,000,000, freezing of bank accounts and referral to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) for criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal fines up to B/. 50,000, asset forfeiture for unexplained wealth, and imprisonment up to 10 years for money laundering offenses connected to the factory's payment flows.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border related-party purchases or sales above the USD 1,000,000 threshold without a comparability study, application of an unapproved method, or omission of the Transfer Pricing Annex from Form 851.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI re-determination of prices at arm's length, automatic upward adjustment of 10% on undocumented cross-border transaction values, plus 5% monthly surcharge and 1% monthly interest on the resulting tax deficiency; repeated non-compliance triggers an audit referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized the non-documented pricing are jointly liable for the deficiency and surcharge and may be disqualified from acting as the PIF's legal representative during DGI enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to foreign shareholders at a treaty-reduced rate without a valid TRC and DGI authorization, or failure to withhold the statutory 10%/5% dividend tax and the 12.5% royalty/interest WHT on Panamanian-source payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The PIF as withholding agent is liable for the full unwithheld amount, a 50% enforcement surcharge, monthly interest at 1%, and an administrative fine between B/. 1,000 and B/. 10,000; if unpaid, the tax becomes an enforceable lien against the factory assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the foundation council are personally liable for maladministered withholding taxes; deliberate under-withholding or misclassification of dividends as loan repayments constitutes fiscal fraud and may lead to criminal conviction and personal asset seizure.
